title: Belly of the Beast

beats.what: Boyd uses his blood infection to kill the night creature; Kristi decides to bring the body inside for study
Fatima confirms her pregnancy to Kristi and asks her not to tell Ellis
Kenny presses Boyd about the worms; Kristi prepares to dissect the creature
Donna confronts Dale about the stabbing; he is unrepentant; she locks him in his room
Jim and Julie argue about Victor and the voice on the radio; their worldviews diverge sharply
Donna tells Fatima: a miracle is just the other side of a nightmare
Donna reveals to Fatima she is pregnant in a town that feeds on pain; Donna reframes it as a possible miracle
Jade and Donna begin dissecting the creature; Kenny refuses to assist and walks out
Kenny tells Kristi he cannot watch her risk her life; he leaves the room
The dissected creature reanimates; Marielle is nearly killed; Boyd shoots it and the creature drops dead again
Kristi and Boyd extract bile from the creature as a possible weapon
Kenny's informant character mentions a music box dream; seeds the next threat

character_beats.beat: Wants a scientific foothold against the creatures; pushes forward with the dissection despite Kenny's fear, taking a risk whose magnitude she cannot yet measure
Wants to protect Kristi and keep order; refuses to participate in an act he believes is reckless, choosing withdrawal over confrontation
Wants a logical, human-scale explanation for the town; when Julie counters every rational theory he retreats to the breakfast table rather than update his model

key_lines.line: A miracle is just the other side of a nightmare.
key_lines.why: Donna gives Fatima a frame for the impossible pregnancy that also applies to the whole season

key_lines.line: I can't go in there and watch you do something that might get you killed.
key_lines.why: Kenny names the exact gap between love and solidarity that drives his exit

key_lines.line: I'm not worried about the monster. I'm worried about the thing that killed it.
key_lines.why: Inverts the episode's danger source: Boyd's worm-derived power is more frightening than the creature

key_lines.line: That thing in the basement came alive, and I think there was a music box.
key_lines.why: First mention of the music box as a dream element; plants the season's closing threat

open_loops: Can the extracted bile actually kill the creatures, or will it have unpredicted effects?
What happened to the worms Boyd expelled: are they still present in the creature's body?
Does the music box that appears in the dream have a physical correlate inside the town?
How long can Fatima keep the pregnancy from Ellis given the escalating danger?
Will Kenny's refusal to assist Kristi permanently fracture their relationship?

payoffs.what: The infected blood Boyd introduced kills the creature; his gamble is confirmed effective
Pregnancy confirmed; Fatima explicitly frames it as medically impossible, raising the stakes of the reveal

contradiction.wants: to stay close to Kristi and protect her at any cost
contradiction.does: abandons her at the dissection table precisely when she needs him most, choosing self-protection over presence

tone_notes: The longest silence of the episode (2:03-8:15, over 131 seconds) separates the creature kill from the morning aftermath, functioning as a hard act break. The episode's two density spikes above 150 w/min occur at minutes 4-5 (creature decision) and 28-29 (dissection crisis/Kenny exit). The final minutes drop under 10 w/min, giving the music box dream revelation an almost inaudible quality that contrasts with the earlier visceral action.
